intention: When something goes wrong, the picture of what just happened is already on disk. Every component logs its major boundary crossings and state changes - an inference call starting, a probe firing at a gate crossing, never every function call or every heartbeat - to one durable logs tree at ~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/, whose interior mirrors the code tree. The diagnostic_inspector reads that tree as its prebuild-for-debugging surface, and one deletion against one root forgets everything older than 30 days.
why: AKIEN, 2026-08-18, verbatim: 'logs are indeed the very next thing we have to look at. because we don't have any. and we should have lots... every single everyting is supposed to log major boundry crossings and state changes... the logs are the picture of what just happened when we have a problem... i went straight from ground loop to things much higher up because i was an idiot and just assumed this part was working.' MEASURED THE SAME DAY, and it refines his claim rather than merely confirming it: the corpus already TRIES to log lots. 14 devices stand in class-space; 15 components already call emit() at boundary crossings (bus, trouble, tester, librarian, web_server, sudo_relay, system_rackmount, intention_extractor, ground_loop, charter/projector, build_inspector...); and there are exactly 3 production set_diagnostic_receiver sites, only 2 of them a disk sink, BOTH inside cairn/devices/ground_loop/__main__.py. So exactly TWO trails exist on disk - ~/.cairn/devices/bus/0/diagnostics.jsonl (311 lines) and ~/.cairn/devices/ground_loop/0/diagnostics.jsonl (168 lines). Every other component's emissions are HELD IN MEMORY by DiagnosticBase (the receiver defaults to None) and die with the process, and nothing anywhere is loud about that. THE LIVED SYMPTOM is the one Akien names: a mind arriving at a red has no picture of what just happened, so it re-explores - which is the exact cost diagnostic_inspector's charter exists to remove ('save you tokens in exploring the issue in the same way the prebuild step does for coding'). THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: wiring the sink is a per-__main__ courtesy instead of physics, so logging is opt-in per assembly point and almost nothing opted in.
how: WIRE, DO NOT BUILD - the parts exist and are proven, and the frame 'build logging' was wrong. The emit surface is cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py (DiagnosticBase, composed into BaseDevice so emit() is structural for every device). The durable sink is BreadcrumbLog (cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/log.py, ticket a-record-reaches-disk, 2026-08-12). The reader is cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector, whose charter already carries Akien's prebuild-for-debugging remit verbatim. Four seams, in dependency order, one per child: (1) the logs tree gains an address at the one owner; (2) a device's emissions reach disk by construction rather than by a wiring call - the physics, Law 4; (3) inference_domain gains an emitter so an inference call starting can log at all (today: zero emit sites); (4) the tree forgets after 30 days by one deletion against one root. MEASURED AND LOAD-BEARING for (2): lowering the writer to the floor is import-legal - log.py imports exactly json, pathlib and cairn.tools.base.address, so its only non-stdlib dependency IS the floor, and diagnostic.py's boot-order law ('stdlib only, no DB, no loguru, no sink backend') forbids a backend, not a json-lines append.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces - DiagnosticBase was born from system_rackmount going red 2/5 SILENTLY, with no assertion and no trace, and a surface that holds its records in memory until the process dies is that same silence one layer along). Law 3 (nothing is known until measured - the emission IS the measurement, and an emission that never reaches disk is a measurement taken and discarded). Law 1 via diagnostic_inspector's charter (the prebuild analog for debugging: the resolver spent only on the novel diagnosis, never on a second exploration to gather what the first pass should have carried). Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics - 'everything logs its boundary crossings' is prose today and opt-in per assembly point, which is exactly the IOU shape). And the standing intention I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass.
gates: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED, and feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs the proofs beside each touched component - cairn/tools/base/ for the address and the floor receiver, cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/ for the reader half - with at least one tooth a hollow build could not pass: a device instantiated with NO wiring act whose emission is then found ON DISK by reading the file, never by asking the object whether it logged. WATCH GATE: WATCHME(every_boundary_crossing_lands_in_the_logs_tree), spec in `watchme`, probe armed at the berth it names. PARENT GATE: the four children prove before this parent crosses PROVED.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a device instance that nobody wired writes its boundary crossings to disk on its first run - the coverage measure being trails-on-disk against components-that-emit, standing at 2 against 15 the day this was cast; (2) starting an inference call leaves a log entry, Akien's own named example, which cannot happen today at all; (3) a probe firing at a gate crossing leaves one; (4) the trails resolve under one root, ~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/, addressed through the one owner and never hand-spelled; (5) deleting everything over 30 days old is ONE deletion against ONE root, crossing no device's gate. WRONG INTENT if: the trails exist and diagnostic_inspector still needs a second exploration to diagnose a red (logging happened, the picture did not - the grain was wrong); or the tree grows write-only with no reader ever firing, which is the slates' measured 96-stored-against-1-read shape re-happening on disk and would mean the inspector's remit went unbought.
horizon: the next red that sends a mind looking for what just happened - the event that reliably tests whether the picture is there - and no later than the inference-ticket reshape, which berths its task ticket in this tree and therefore cannot land honestly before it.
children: FOUR, in dependency order, each with its own address and its own proof; they prove before this parent. (1) the-logs-tree-has-one-address - cairn/tools/base/address.py gains a LOGS segment and log_path(device, instance) resolving instance/logs/<device>/<instance>/, with the index-not-ownership distinction recorded there beside the 2026-08-12 ruling it reconciles. Lands FIRST: everything else addresses through it, and wiring more devices before it would mint more trails at the old root. (2) a-device-logs-without-being-wired - the heart and the physics: the writer reaches the floor and a device's emissions reach disk by construction. Settles the three candidate shapes named in distinctions_recorded. (3) an-inference-call-logs-that-it-started - inference_domain gains an emitter; carries the device-ness question and is the rung the inference-ticket reshape stands on. (4) the-logs-tree-forgets-after-30-days - the sweep over the one root, carrying the learns-its-gates edge on the constant. Deliberately NOT decomposed further: the emit surface needs no work at all, which is why this cast builds almost no new mechanism.

watchme.trigger: each firing of the probe over the logs tree - it rides the device walk that already exists (ground_loop discovery enumerates class-space device folders) rather than a clock, and it needs no live host and no inference: the two populations it compares are files on disk and emit sites in the corpus.
watchme.enough: NOT satisfied by the corpus it was written against. Enough when the invariant has held across at least TWO device births that came AFTER this ticket landed - a device added later, logging on its first run with nobody having wired it - because a floor proved by the callers that already exist is a claim about nothing. Same enough-clause shape as a-standing-table-gains-its-constraint-through-the-one-door, deliberately borrowed.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying the two counts it compares (components that emit, trails that exist) as measured values rather than as a pass word - so a later reader sees the coverage move rather than reading that it was fine.
watchme.nexus: the diagnostic nexus - what a mind needs on disk to diagnose a red without a second exploration; it teaches the same tree diagnostic_inspector's filters read, which is where 'what did we need and not have' accumulates.
watchme.consumer: CC at the moment of a red (through diagnostic_inspector, the prebuild-for-debugging surface), and Akien at the session-open banner when coverage regresses.

provenance: Born at /intent 2026-08-18 from Akien's statement captured verbatim in CairnCommons/ideas/2026-08-18-for-now-only-graph-trees-are-in.json, which arrived mid-review while the inference-ticket reshape was being sequenced. It reached /intent rather than the ticket entry point because it is not a bug: nothing here is broken code to edit, it is an intention ('every single everyting is supposed to log') that was never wired into physics. THE FIRING CHANGED ITS OWN FRAME: Akien's opening claim was 'we don't have any [logs]', and his own addendum minutes later - 'indeed, perhaps i just didn't know where to look' - is the corrected one. The census found the tool, the sink and the reader all present and proven; what was absent was the wiring. So this is a wiring ticket wearing a building ticket's clothes, and the four children are small because of it.
distinctions_recorded: THE COLLIDING RULING IS AKIEN'S OWN, AND IT RESOLVES IN HIS FAVOUR TWICE OVER. cairn/tools/base/address.py:20-33 records his 2026-08-12 ownership test: 'THE TOP LEVEL OF ~/.cairn/ IS FOR WHAT IS NOT ANY DEVICE'S STATE... the test is not depth, it is OWNERSHIP: a file that answers "what is true of this machine" lives at the top; a file that answers "what is true of this device" lives under devices/<name>/<instance>/.' A device's diagnostic trail answers what is true of that DEVICE, which is why BreadcrumbLog writes to ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/diagnostics.jsonl - the built address is a faithful translation of the 08-12 ruling, not drift. His 2026-08-18 statement puts it under a top-level logs/ root instead. NOT EXCLUSIVE-AND-TERMINAL, and the reconciliation is inside the 08-12 ruling's own words: it names logs top-level in the same breath as venv ('~/.cairn/venv is correct - ONE venv per box, never one per device, and the same for logs and backups'). So 08-12 settled that logs IS a root; 08-18 settles its interior shape and gives the why. The two compose. THE RESIDUAL TENSION - device state living outside the device's space - dissolves on the ownership test itself: the <device>/<instance>/ segments beneath logs/ are an INDEX, not an ownership claim, and mirroring the code tree is addressing rather than owning.

THE RETENTION WHY MAKES THE NEW SHAPE PROTECT LAW 6 RATHER THAN STRAIN IT, and this is the argument that turns Akien's stated convenience ('easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go') into a structural reason. address.py bounds itself explicitly: 'a shared helper that reached into every device's space to CREATE would be that failure written once and called convenient.' A 30-day sweep is that same reach in the DELETE direction, and delete is the more dangerous half. With trails scattered under 14 devices' own spaces the sweep must cross 14 gates; with one logs root it crosses none, because the logs root is nobody's device space. The convenience and the law want the same shape.

WHERE THE DEFAULT RECEIVER INSTALLS IS NOT SETTLED BY THIS CAST, and it is recorded as un-wrapped rather than smoothed over. Three shapes stand: (a) BaseDevice.__init__ wires a default receiver with a function-local import, keeping the module top import-light; (b) the writer LOWERS to cairn/tools/base/ as a floor-legal leaf and DiagnosticBase defaults to it, diagnostic_inspector keeping the reader half; (c) injection stays and every assembly point calls set_diagnostic_receiver. (c) IS ALREADY FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT - it is today's design, and it produced 3 production wiring sites against 15 emitting components. (b) is favoured on an in-house precedent of the identical shape, recorded in address.py itself: the roots table was 'Lowered here from cairn/machines/skill_block/counters.py on 2026-08-12 - the table was already injectable and already carried the why; what it lacked was an address the rest of the system could stand on.' BreadcrumbLog is in exactly that position. Favouring is not settling: the child a-device-logs-without-being-wired settles it against its own falsifier.

THE GRAIN IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A RULE, and nothing in this cast derives it. Akien drew the line by example - 'that doesn't mean every function call, or every heartbeat from the ground loop... but starting an inference call sure should. a probe firing at a gate crossing should' - so each emitter judges its own boundary crossings. This is left standing deliberately: a taxonomy of what-counts-as-major written now would be the reification failure this system keeps catching, and the falsifier's second arm (the inspector still needing a second exploration) is what would tell us the grain was wrong. If it goes wrong, the fix is evidence about real diagnoses, not a rule written in advance.

A NON-DEVICE CANNOT EMIT TODAY, and that is why the inference emitter is its own child. emit() arrives by inheriting BaseDevice; inference_domain is module functions and has zero emit sites, so Akien's flagship example - an inference call starting should log - is the one case the existing mechanism cannot reach at all. Giving it an emitter touches the standing open question open-what-grants-device-ness-once-definition-location-stops-being-evidence, which this intent did not mean to open and must not answer by accident.
